newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf sale brings 96 selloffs to 27 bln Ff.
newsitem.headline: Elf sale brings 96 selloffs to 27 bln Ff.

text.p: The French government's sale of a stake in oil company Elf Aquitaine on Wednesday brought total revenues from privatisations this year to 27 billion francs, government spokesman Alain Lamassoure said.
He told reporters after a weekly cabinet meeting that the government had originally planned to raise 22 billion francs this year. "After Elf, we will have 27 billion," he said.
The government said earlier it was selling a nine percent stake in Elf Aquitaine -- most of the remaining stake which it retained when the oil company was privatised in 1994 -- for 10 billion francs.
The money will top up funds needed to provide capital injections into state-owned companies.
On top of the 27 billion francs in privatisation receipts available for capital injections this year, a total 8.7 billion francs is also to be provided from central government budget funds.
This includes an additional 4.9 billion francs in a revised budget for 1996 approved by the government on Wednesday.
Lamassoure said 13 billion francs had already been spent on capital injections this year, going to Air France, arms maker GIAT, regional bank Societe Marseillaise de Credit and Cie Generale Maritime.

"That leaves 23 billion francs which will therefore be shared out between now and the end of the year between companies which need to be recapitalised, particularly those that are in the course of being privatised," he said.
He declined to name the companies involved.

State-owned Thomson SA is due to have an 11 billion franc recapitalisation before it is sold to Lagardere Groupe, while the government may need to spend up to 2.6 billion francs to pay for a managed wind-down of property lender Credit Foncier de France.
State bank Credit Lyonnais may need more than 10 billion francs in a capital injection in the years ahead to ready it for privatisation, banking analysts estimate.
